name: Dutch colonial empire (1796–1975)
capital: The Hague; Batavia (Jakarta) in the East Indies
summary: The Netherlands’ colonies after the Dutch East India Company: above all the Dutch East Indies (Indonesia), plus Suriname and Caribbean islands. Indonesia won independence in 1945–49.

knownFor.label: Cultivation System
knownFor.note: Javanese farmers were forced to grow export crops for the Dutch.

knownFor.label: Max Havelaar
knownFor.note: A novel by Multatuli criticising colonial abuse.

knownFor.label: Batik
knownFor.note: Javanese wax-resist dyed cloth, traded worldwide.

location.value: The Indonesian archipelago, Suriname and the Dutch Caribbean.
location.source: Wikipedia: Dutch East Indies; Wikipedia: Dutch colonial empire

terrain.value: Tropical islands, coasts and river deltas.
terrain.source: Wikipedia: Dutch East Indies; Wikipedia: Dutch colonial empire

climate.source: Wikipedia: Dutch East Indies; Wikipedia: Dutch colonial empire

resources.value: Spices, coffee, sugar, rubber, tin and oil.
resources.source: Wikipedia: Dutch East Indies; Wikipedia: Dutch colonial empire

disasters.value: The 1883 Krakatoa eruption preceded the Banten Peasants’ Revolt; the article gives no death toll.

urbanisation.value: Batavia (now Jakarta) was the colonial capital.

disease.value: Cholera and famine; plantations had harsh conditions.
disease.source: Wikipedia: Dutch East Indies; Wikipedia: Dutch colonial empire

migration.value: Javanese workers were sent to Suriname from 1890, and Indian workers also went.
migration.source: Wikipedia: Dutch East Indies; Wikipedia: Dutch colonial empire

economicBase.value: Export plantations (sugar, coffee, rubber), mining and oil.
economicBase.source: Wikipedia: Dutch East Indies; Wikipedia: Dutch colonial empire

tradeRoutes.value: Shipping between the Netherlands and Asia; the Suez route after 1869.
tradeRoutes.source: Wikipedia: Dutch East Indies; Wikipedia: Dutch colonial empire

wealth.value: Colonial profits were a large part of Dutch state income in the 19th century.
wealth.source: Wikipedia: Dutch East Indies; Wikipedia: Dutch colonial empire

moneyAndTax.value: The guilder; 840 million guilders were taken from the East Indies between 1830 and 1870.

inequality.value: A rigid social and racial caste system; a legal classification of “Foreign Orientals” (Arabs and Chinese).

governmentType.value: A governor-general ruled the Dutch East Indies under the Dutch crown.
governmentType.source: Wikipedia: Dutch East Indies; Wikipedia: Dutch colonial empire

keyRulers.value: Herman Willem Daendels (Governor-General from 1808). Johannes van den Bosch (Governor-General 1830–1835; the Cultivation System).

succession.value: Governors were appointed in the Netherlands.
succession.source: Wikipedia: Dutch East Indies; Wikipedia: Dutch colonial empire

institutions.value: Colonial administration and courts, with local rulers kept in place in some regions.
institutions.source: Wikipedia: Dutch East Indies; Wikipedia: Dutch colonial empire

stability.value: The Java War (1825–30); the Aceh War (infobox 1873–1904; the body gives the Acehnese surrender as 1912).

eliteConflict.value: Debates in the Netherlands over the “Ethical Policy” (from 1901).
eliteConflict.source: Wikipedia: Dutch East Indies; Wikipedia: Dutch colonial empire

armyAndTech.value: The Royal Netherlands East Indies Army (KNIL), established in 1814; its air arm ML-KNIL dates from 1915.

majorWars.value: Java War (1825–30) and Aceh War; Japanese occupation (1942–45; the KNIL surrendered on Java on 8 March 1942); Indonesian National Revolution (1945–49).

territoryChange.value: Lost Indonesia (1949), West New Guinea (1962) and Suriname (1975).
territoryChange.source: Wikipedia: Dutch East Indies; Wikipedia: Dutch colonial empire

alliancesRivals.value: Allied with Britain in the Napoleonic era.
alliancesRivals.source: Wikipedia: Dutch East Indies; Wikipedia: Dutch colonial empire

inventions.source: Wikipedia: Dutch East Indies; Wikipedia: Dutch colonial empire

scienceEducation.value: Limited schooling for Indonesians until the 20th century.
scienceEducation.source: Wikipedia: Dutch East Indies; Wikipedia: Dutch colonial empire

openness.value: Closed: political rights were limited for the colonised.
openness.source: Wikipedia: Dutch East Indies; Wikipedia: Dutch colonial empire

communicationTransport.value: The Great Post Road across Java was built under Daendels (appointed 1808; the article does not date the road).

religion.value: Islam, Christianity and local religions among the colonised.
religion.source: Wikipedia: Dutch East Indies; Wikipedia: Dutch colonial empire

languageWriting.value: Dutch was used by the administration, and Malay became the base of Indonesian.
languageWriting.source: Wikipedia: Dutch East Indies; Wikipedia: Dutch colonial empire

artsArchitecture.source: Wikipedia: Dutch East Indies; Wikipedia: Dutch colonial empire

socialStructure.value: A racial hierarchy of Europeans, then “foreign orientals” and “natives”.
socialStructure.source: Wikipedia: Dutch East Indies; Wikipedia: Dutch colonial empire

sharedIdentity.value: A growing Indonesian nationalism in the 1900s.
sharedIdentity.source: Wikipedia: Dutch East Indies; Wikipedia: Dutch colonial empire

dailyLife.value: Colonists in villas; most people in villages; rice and spices.
dailyLife.source: Wikipedia: Dutch East Indies; Wikipedia: Dutch colonial empire

neighbours.value: British Malaya, Portuguese Timor and Australian New Guinea.
neighbours.source: Wikipedia: Dutch East Indies; Wikipedia: Dutch colonial empire

ideasReligions.value: Nationalist ideas grew in Dutch-run schools.
ideasReligions.source: Wikipedia: Dutch East Indies; Wikipedia: Dutch colonial empire

colonisation.value: A colonial empire, with forced cultivation and labour in the 1800s.
colonisation.source: Wikipedia: Dutch East Indies; Wikipedia: Dutch colonial empire

riseSignals.value: Direct Dutch control from 31 December 1799 (infobox); the body says the VOC was formally dissolved in 1800.

peakPeriod.value: Around 1900–1930, when Dutch control reached its widest extent.
peakPeriod.source: Wikipedia: Dutch East Indies; Wikipedia: Dutch colonial empire

declineSignals.value: Japanese occupation (1942–45); independence declared on 17 August 1945.

outcome.value: Ended with Indonesian (1949) and Suriname (1975) independence.
outcome.source: Wikipedia: Dutch East Indies; Wikipedia: Dutch colonial empire

sources.value: Wikipedia: Dutch East Indies; Wikipedia: Dutch colonial empire.
sources.source: Wikipedia: Dutch East Indies; Wikipedia: Dutch colonial empire
